claims.text: The Prometheus server scrapes: every scrape_interval it sends an HTTP GET to each configured target's metrics path and stores the returned samples with the scrape's timestamp (pull model; the target does not push).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Overview (pull model); Configuration (scrape_config, scrape_interval)

claims.text: deploy/monitoring/prometheus.yml@stage-2:1-11: global scrape_interval 5s; one scrape_config job_name api with static_configs targets ["api:8080"].
metrics_path defaults to /metrics, so a target written as api:8080 is scraped at http://api:8080/metrics.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Configuration, scrape_config metrics_path default; outputs/stage-2/scripts/devops/prometheus-targets.txt (url=http://api:8080/metrics)

claims.text: Prometheus attaches the job_name as label job="api" to series scraped from that job's targets.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Jobs and instances (automatically generated labels: job, instance)

claims.text: For every scraped target Prometheus records the series up: 1 if the target is healthy (scrape succeeded), 0 if the scrape failed; a stopped API gives up 0.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Jobs and instances (up{job, instance}); outputs/stage-2/scripts/devops/prometheus-targets.txt

claims.text: A time series is identified by its metric name and set of label values; each distinct combination is its own series, and each successful scrape appends one timestamped sample to each.
Labels with unbounded values (user ids, order ids) create a new series per value and should be avoided (cardinality).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Naming (labels: do not use for high-cardinality values such as user IDs); Data model caution

claims.text: docker-compose.yml@stage-2: prometheus, grafana, loki, alloy carry profiles: [monitoring]; a plain docker compose up (as run by scripts/up.sh) leaves them out; docker compose --profile monitoring up -d starts them too.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Compose profiles (Using profiles with Compose); examples/don-hang @ stage-2: docker-compose.yml:237-253, scripts/up.sh:16

claims.text: The prometheus service mounts ./deploy/monitoring/prometheus.yml at /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml (read-only), publishes 9090, and sits on the donhang network (172.28.0.21), so it reaches api:8080 without Caddy.

Prometheus's HTTP API: GET /api/v1/targets lists activeTargets with labels.job, scrapeUrl, scrapeInterval, health (up/down); GET /api/v1/query returns data.result[].value [time, value]; the script's jq runs in the lab box (docker compose exec -T lab jq).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: HTTP API (targets, instant queries); scripts/devops/prometheus-targets.sh @ stage-2 lines 9-13, 23

claims.text: scripts/devops/prometheus-targets.sh@stage-2 output: job=api url=http://api:8080/metrics interval=5s health=up; up 1; after docker compose stop api: up 0, health=down; the EXIT trap starts api again and waits for up 1.
Prometheus never reads container output: it gets metrics only from HTTP scrapes of the targets in its configuration.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Overview (pull over HTTP); deploy/monitoring/prometheus.yml @ stage-2
